purpose: Engineering failures and measured limitations are part of the reproducibility record, not noise to be deleted.

entries.failure: launcher process guard used a full-command-line match (pgrep -f), which matched the bash wrapper whose command text CONTAINED the script — false-positive 'run already active'
entries.effect: the watchdog would have refused every legitimate restart; with the host recycling every ~3 h, no corridor run would ever have advanced again
entries.detection: manual audit during a watchdog tick (launcher reported a run active while ps showed no python3 solver)
entries.correction: guard now matches only real python3 processes (ps comm=='python3' AND args ~ run_corridor.py)

entries.failure: corridor_analysis.py labelled a partial run FINAL because a stale meta.json from a short smoke test satisfied the completeness check
entries.effect: a partial probe series could have been reported as a final result
entries.detection: self-review of the first analysis output
entries.correction: completeness now requires the probe series to actually reach the run's target window
entries.affected_scientific_results: none — caught before any partial output was used in a claim

entries.failure: probe scheduler deadline (_next) was restored as time+interval instead of its saved value
entries.effect: a restart could silently skip one probe sample and shift the probe grid; probe continuity LOOKED fine while the schedule drifted
entries.detection: state audit prompted by external review before the wet-phase equivalence test
entries.correction: _next is now saved in and restored from the checkpoint; the wet-phase A/B test compares every probe record bitwise
entries.affected_scientific_results: none for completed analyses (all published probe series came from runs without a mid-interval restart of this kind)

entries.measured_limitation: the solver executes on ONE core (~100% CPU measured via /proc jiffies: 999/10 s), not four — elementwise NumPy kernels do not use BLAS threading
entries.consequence: sequential scheduling buys restart robustness and memory headroom, not compute acceleration; wall-time projections must assume single-core throughput
entries.decision: solver is NOT being rewritten or parallelized mid-experiment; the limitation is recorded instead
